```{r}
#| include: false

### Download data
url_RONI <- "https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/RONI.ascii.txt"

# Read the data table into a data frame
# The file uses whitespace to separate Season, Year, and RONI index value
RONI_full <- read.table(
  url_RONI,
  comment.char = '#',
  header = T,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Optional save
#write.csv(RONI_full, file = paste(Dir, '/RONI_', RptYr, '.csv', sep = ""))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
### Round data to the tenth of a degree
RONI_rounded <- round(RONI_full$ANOM, digits = 1)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
# Note that the above needs to be 'echo' and not 'include' so that the error checks print.

# Pull out the values we need for the report 
yr_of_int <- which(RONI_full$YR == RptYr)
prev_yrs <- which(RONI_full$YR < RptYr)
all_yrs <- which(RONI_full$YR <= RptYr)
monthly_min_RptYr <- min(RONI_full$ANOM[yr_of_int])
monthly_min_PrevYrs <- min(RONI_full$ANOM[prev_yrs])
monthly_max_RptYr <- max(RONI_full$ANOM[yr_of_int])
monthly_max_PrevYrs <- max(RONI_full$ANOM[prev_yrs])

if (monthly_max_RptYr > monthly_max_PrevYrs) {
  print('The highest monthly value was in the report year.')
}

if (monthly_max_RptYr > monthly_max_PrevYrs) {
  print('The lowest monthly value was in the report year.')
}
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# Write csv for dashboard
# Note that dashboard output has its own folder
# Thanks to Emily Conklin for this chunk of code!

month_list <- c("DJF", "JFM", "FMA", "MAM", "AMJ", "MJJ", 
                "JJA", "JAS", "ASO", "SON", "OND", "NDJ")

ENSO_dashboard <- RONI_full %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(Month = which(month_list == SEAS)) %>%
  mutate(Date_Time = paste0("15-", Month, "-", as.character(YR), " 00:00")) %>%
  mutate(Value_lm = NA, Anom = NA, Anom_lm = NA, ID = "ENSO", Units = "Relative Oceanic Nino Index") %>%
  select(Date_Time, Year = YR, Month, Value = ANOM, Anom, ID, Value_lm, Anom_lm, Units) |>
  filter(Year <= RptYr)

#write_csv(ENSO_dashboard, file = here("Indicator_Dashboard", "Data", paste('ENSO_Dashboard_Data_', RptYr, '.csv', sep = "")))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# Borrowing code from the dashboard for this chunk
# so that figures look the same across products
indicator_data <- ENSO_dashboard |>
  filter(Year <= RptYr) %>% 
  mutate(Date_Time=dmy_hm(Date_Time))

# Create color palette for easy reference 
pal <- c(coral[2], oceans[2], ann_grey)

# Calculate pos/neg/neutral ENSO values 
# Needs to be greater than 0.5 or less than -0.5 for at least five consecutive seasons
indicator_data <- indicator_data |> mutate(Sign = sign(Value)) |>
  mutate(Sign = ifelse(test = (Value < 0.5 & Value > -0.5), yes = 0, no = Sign)) |> # positive or negative?
  group_by(Sign, Group = with(rle(Sign), rep(seq_along(lengths), lengths))) |> # how many seasons in a row?
  ungroup() |>
  add_count(Group) |>
  mutate(ENSO = ifelse(Sign == -1 & n >= 5, 
                       yes = 'La Niña', 
                       no = ifelse(Sign == 1 & n >= 5, 
                                   yes = 'El Niño', 
                                   no = 'Neutral'))) |> 
  mutate(Units = "Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI)")

# x axis ticks and grid
x_grid <- c(seq.POSIXt(min(indicator_data$Date_Time), max(indicator_data$Date_Time), by='10 year'),
            max(indicator_data$Date_Time))

# Adding figure specific looks to the base theme listed in _common.R 
plotTheme <- plotTheme + 
  theme(legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = 'inside', 
        legend.position.inside = c(0.95,0.92),
        legend.text = element_text(size=12), 
        legend.key.spacing.x = unit(1.5,'cm'),
        legend.spacing.y = unit(0.1,'cm'))

# Make stem type plot using ggplot
p <- ggplot(indicator_data) + 
  geom_segment(aes(x = Date_Time, y = 0, xend = Date_Time, yend = Value, colour = ENSO), linewidth = 0.3) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = pal, name=NULL) + 
  scale_x_datetime(breaks = x_grid, date_labels = '%Y', expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  ylim(c(-3,3)) +
  xlab('Year') +
  ylab('Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI)') +
  plotTheme +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 3), byrow=T))  # Make the lines in the legend thicker

```

p

**Rationale:** The El Niño – Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle is known to have impacts on Pacific fisheries including tuna fisheries. The ONI focuses on ocean temperature, which has the most direct effect on these fisheries.   
\
**Status:** The Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) remained in largely neutral conditions in `r RptYr`. In `r RptYr`, the RONI ranged from `r monthly_min_RptYr` to `r monthly_max_RptYr`.  This is within the range of values observed previously in the time series.  
\
**Description:** The three-month running mean (referred to as a season) of satellite remotely-sensed sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region (5°S – 5°N, 120° – 170°W). The Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) is a measure of the El Niño – Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phase. Warm and cool phases, termed El Niño and La Niña respectively, are based in part on an RONI threshold of ± 0.5 °C being met for a minimum of five consecutive overlapping seasons. Additional atmospheric indices are needed to confirm an El Niño or La Niña event, as the ENSO is a coupled ocean-atmosphere phenomenon. The atmospheric half of ENSO is measured using the Southern Oscillation Index. **NOTE: In February 2026 the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) was replaced by the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) as NOAAs official index to track ENSO. ONI measures temperature departures (SST anomalies) in one Pacific region (Niño‑3.4). RONI measures those departures relative to the departures across the broader tropical oceans, which better represents the physics that drive ENSO impacts. 2026 is the first year RONI is being used in the SAFE report.**
\
**Timeframe:** Three-month running average.  
\
**Region/Location:** Niño3.4 region, 5°S – 5°N, 120° – 170°W.  
\
**Measurement Platform:** *In-situ* station, satellite, model.  
\
**Data available at:** <https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/RONI.ascii.txt>.   
\
**Sourced from:** @NOAA-CPC2026-sc. Graphics produced in part using @Stawitz2026-kw.
